task: Build an inventory and orders app with an API, tests and a dark page; use it in a browser. Mid-run: add a low-stock badge. Then: a PDF sales report.

steps.title: Type the brief
steps.detail: Six parts: a Flask and SQLite shop, a JSON API, a dark page, pytest tests, then two orders placed through the page.

steps.title: Its own sealed box
steps.detail: The session gets its own gVisor box on the Vultr worker. No keys inside, no route to private networks.

steps.title: Install what's missing
steps.detail: Flask isn't in the box, so it installs Flask and pytest itself.

steps.title: Write the app and tests
steps.detail: app.py with SQLite and the API (409 when stock runs out), the page, and 6 pytest tests. All pass.

steps.title: Start it and use it
steps.detail: It starts the server, checks the API answers, opens the page in the box's browser and orders a keyboard.

steps.title: We steer it mid-run
steps.detail: We send a second message while it works: add a red Low stock badge, test it, restart, check the page.

steps.title: Badge and a 7th test
steps.detail: It reads its own code, adds the badge and a seventh test, and runs the suite: 7 passed.

steps.title: Restart and prove it
steps.detail: It restarts the app, orders 20 keyboards through the form, and checks the page now says Low stock.

steps.title: Screenshot, answer
steps.detail: Screenshot taken, tests re-run, first answer posted: 43 seconds for the whole first turn.

steps.title: A follow-up turn
steps.detail: We ask for a one-page A4 PDF report. Same box, same database: it carries on where it stopped.

steps.title: Query the database
steps.detail: There's no sqlite3 command in the box, so it queries with Python: 2 orders, $1,889.79.

steps.title: Draw the PDF
steps.detail: reportlab isn't installed, so it draws the page with matplotlib: total, orders table, revenue chart.

steps.title: Check it fits
steps.detail: It measures the PDF with PyMuPDF: everything inside the A4 page. The table is cramped, though.

steps.title: Done
steps.detail: 70 s of agent time over two turns, 37 tool calls, 39 model calls on Vultr: $0.016.

steps.title: Open the files
steps.detail: The Files panel shows the workspace: the app, its database, tests, screenshot and report.pdf.

results.label: THE AGENT'S OWN SCREENSHOT
results.caption: After the mid-run message: 20 keyboards ordered, stock 4, the Low stock badge on the page.

results.label: THE FOLLOW-UP: report.pdf
results.caption: One A4 page from the database. It fits the page; its table is cramped.

replay_story: An agent in its own sandbox on Vultr builds a Flask and SQLite shop with an API, tests and a dark page, then uses it in a real browser. While it works we tell it to add a low-stock badge, and afterwards we ask for a PDF sales report. Every step below is from the session's own event log. Pick one to jump the recording to it.

replay_results.caption: The agent's screenshot after the mid-run message: 20 keyboards ordered through the form, stock 4, and the Low stock badge.
replay_results.alt: The shop page: a products table with a red Low stock badge next to Mechanical Keyboard, and an order form.

replay_results.caption: report.pdf from the follow-up turn: total revenue, the two orders and a revenue chart on one A4 page. It fits the page, but the table's columns are cramped.
replay_results.alt: A one-page sales report with a total, a small orders table and a single gold bar.

replay_notes: A script drove a headless browser against the live web chat: it typed the brief, sent the low-stock message while the agent was still working, sent the PDF request after the first answer, then opened the Files panel. The recording plays in real time; the 1×, 2× and 4× buttons only change how you watch it.
The event times come from the session's own log, and the recording is lined up with them at the moment the first message reached the server, to within about half a second.

This is the second recording of this brief. In the first, the agent added the badge without restarting the server, then said the badge showed in its screenshot when it did not. The low-stock message was then made to ask for a restart and a check on the page, and the session was recorded again. Both are in the repository's evidence folder.
Agent errors are left in: a missing python command, a wrong file path, no sqlite3 binary, no reportlab. Each one shows as a failed or retried step, with what came back.
